metadata.title: How to Replace the Seats & Springs in a Single Handle Faucet | Repair and Replace
metadata.description:
Is your single handle faucet leaking? In this episode of Repair and Replace, Stephany shows how to replace the seats and springs in a single handle, ball valve style bathroom faucet. If the faucet is leaking, replacing the seats and springs is one way to stop the leak. The rubber seats can wear down over time which can cause the faucet to run continuously.

Replacement part # ULND9
Order seats and springs online https://www.amresupply.com/part/ULND9-DELTA-ST-SPG-ASSY

transcript.text:
Hi I'm Stephany and welcome to
Repair and Replace,
your online resource for quick and easy repairs.

In this episode, I’ll show you exactly how
to replace the seats and springs
in a single handle faucet.
To order online, explore our website below.

To begin, you’ll need seats and springs, 
channel lock pliers, needle nose pliers,
an Allen wrench and a cloth

A single handle faucet uses a small ball valve
to control water flow and temperature.

Two small holes in the ball valve connect
to the hot and cold supply
and make contact the rubber seats.

Over time these seats and springs can wear
down and become leaky.

Replacing the seats and springs is easy and
can save you from replacing the entire faucet.
First, close the shutoff valve.

Turn on the faucet to completely drain the
lines and relieve any built up pressure.

Next, plug your sink so you won’t lose any
pieces during the repair.
First, remove the screw cover.
Use an Allen wrench to remove the set screw.

The Allen wrench size will depend on your
faucet.

This screw holds the handle in place and some
models will need a Phillips screwdriver instead.
Next, pull off the handle.

Use the needle nose pliers to unscrew the
adjusting ring.

Place a cloth over top and use the channel
lock pliers to unscrew the cap.
Now pull out the ball, the cam, and packing.
Soak up the water in the faucet shank.

This will make it easier to remove and installing
the new seats and springs.

Looking down into the faucet, you should see
the seats and springs.

Insert an Allen wrench into the rubber seat
and tilt it slightly to catch the spring underneath.

Lift out to remove and discard the seats and
springs for both sides.
The springs are wedge shaped.

The larger part should be on the bottom with
the rubber seats acting as a cap.

Now insert your new seats and springs in the
holes.
First, install the ball valve.

Align the pin to the slot on the side of the
ball valve and slide the valve in.

Place the cam over top of the packing and
align the tab to the slot.
Next, place the cap on top of the cap.

Push the lever forward and apply pressure
with your thumb to keep the cam in the slot.

This will prevent the cam from rotating out
of place as the cap is screwed on.
Hand tighten the cap.

Now, use the needle nose pliers to screw on
the adjusting ring.

Screw the handle back into place and replace
the screw cap.
Finally, turn the water back.
Test out your faucet and check for any leaks.
If you found this video useful hit "like".

To keep up-to-date on Repair and Replace,
please subscribe

and for the widest selection of parts, low
prices, and same day shipping
explore our website below.
Thanks for watching.

summary.brief: Stephany demonstrates how to replace the seats and springs in a single‑handle ball‑style faucet.
summary.detailed: The video opens with Stephany introducing the repair and showing the required tools, then she closes the shut‑off valve, opens the faucet to flush and drain the lines, and plugs the sink. Using an Allen wrench she removes the set screw, pulls off the handle, unscrews the adjusting ring with needle‑nose pliers, and removes the cap with channel‑lock pliers. She extracts the ball, cam and packing, wipes away water with a cloth, and observes the rubber seats and wedge‑shaped springs inside. Each seat is tilted with an Allen wrench to catch its spring, the old seats and springs are lifted out and discarded, and new seats and springs are installed in the corresponding holes. The ball valve is reinserted, the cam is positioned over the packing and locked in its slot, the cap is hand‑tightened, the adjusting ring is re‑screwed, and the handle is re‑attached with its screw cover. Finally she restores the water supply, tests the faucet for leaks, and ends the tutorial.

action.detailed: Close the water supply, drain the faucet, remove the handle and internal components, lift out the worn rubber seats and wedge‑shaped springs, install new seats and springs, then reassemble the ball valve, cam, cap and handle before restoring water flow.

summary_sent_to_llm.description:
Is your single handle faucet leaking? In this episode of Repair and Replace, Stephany shows how to replace the seats and springs in a single handle, ball valve style bathroom faucet. If the faucet is leaking, replacing the seats and springs is one way to stop the leak. The rubber seats can wear down over time which can cause the faucet to run continuously.

Replacement part # ULND9
Order seats and springs online https://www.amresupply.com/part/ULND9-DELTA-ST-SPG-ASSY

Order the ball and lever here: https://www.amresupply.com/part/ULND2A-DELTA-LEVER-HND-BALL

summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with Stephany introducing the repair and showing the required tools, then she closes the shut‑off valve, opens the faucet to flush and drain the lines, and plugs the sink. Using an Allen wrench she removes the set screw, pulls off the handle, unscrews the adjusting ring with needle‑nose pliers, and removes the cap with channel‑lock pliers. She extracts the ball, cam and packing, wipes away water with a cloth, and observes the rubber seats and wedge‑shaped springs inside. Each seat is tilted with an Allen wrench to catch its spring, the old seats and springs are lifted out and discarded, and new seats and springs are installed in the corresponding holes. The ball valve is reinserted, the cam is positioned over the packing and locked in its slot, the cap is hand‑tightened, the adjusting ring is re‑screwed, and the handle is re‑attached with its screw cover. Finally she restores the water supply, tests the faucet for leaks, and ends the tutorial.
